text.p01: To everyone who asks before they tell. A story about asking instead of telling.
text.p03: On the green banks of the Nile River lived Kemi, a young hoopoe with a fancy orange crest and stripy black-and-white wings.
text.p04: Kemi knew lots of things, and she loved to tell them. Whenever she said, "I know!" her crest popped up like a fan. Pop!
text.p05: She told the kingfisher how to fish. She told the jerboas how to dig. She told the frogs how to croak. "I know! I know!"
text.p06: But she never asked them anything. Little by little, her friends stopped talking when Kemi came near. There wasn't any room for their words.
text.p07: One evening at the desert's edge, Kemi met Sabu, a little beetle rolling a big ball. He kept stopping to look up at the sky.
text.p08: "Roll, roll, look up!" sang Sabu. Kemi's crest popped. "I know! You should push it from the front!" She never asked why he looked up.
text.p09: The next day, Kemi flew over the desert. "I know the desert better than anyone!" she said. She flew and flew, past dune after dune.
text.p10: When the sun went down, every dune looked the same. Which way was home? For the first time ever, Kemi didn't know. Her crest drooped.
text.p11: Then she heard a small song under the stars: "Roll, roll, look up!" It was Sabu! Kemi's crest began to pop. "I kn…"
text.p12: Kemi stopped. She didn't know. So, for the very first time, she asked a question instead. "Sabu, how do you find your way at night?"
text.p13: Sabu's eyes sparkled. Nobody had ever asked him that! "Look up," he said. "See the river of stars? It shows me the way."
text.p14: A soft river of stars stretched across the sky. "Where does it lead?" asked Kemi. "All the way to the great river," said Sabu.
text.p15: Kemi asked another question, and another. Each one opened like a little door. Behind each door was something she had never known.
text.p16: Beetles roll backward, standing on their heads! Sabu's grandma taught him the star song! And Sabu asked questions too: "What's it like to fly?"
text.p17: So they set off together, following the river of stars. Kemi hopped beside Sabu, and they sang all the way. "Roll, roll, look up!"
text.p18: Then a thin cloud slid over the stars. This time, Kemi didn't guess. She thought, "Who could I ask?"
text.p19: Nearby, a jerboa family peeked out of their burrow. Kemi didn't tell them how to dig. She asked, "Which way to the great river, please?"
text.p20: The jerboas' ears shot up. They loved being asked! "We know a shortcut!" they squeaked, and bounced ahead through the dunes. Boing, boing!
text.p21: At the top of the last dune, the cloud slid away. The river of stars sparkled overhead, and below, the great river shone like silver.
text.p22: "I didn't know the way," said Kemi. "But I asked, and asking took me farther than all my telling ever did." Pop! went her crest.
text.p23: Back home, Kemi still knew many things. But now she asked first. "How do you fish?" "How do you dig?" Her friends talked and talked.
text.p24: Whenever she learned something new, even from a beetle, pop! went her crest. Telling shows what you know. Asking helps you grow. The End
text.cover: The Beetle Who Knew the Stars. A Story About Asking Instead of Telling
